stories.headline: Rajnath Singh meets US Secy of War Hegseth on sidelines of ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting in Philippines
stories.title: Rajnath Singh meets US Secy of War Hegseth on sidelines of ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting in Philippines
stories.summary: Philippines, October 28 : Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday met US War Secretary Pete Hegseth on sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines. The Defence Minister is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from the United States, Japan, Australia and from other participating nations. The US War Secretary said during the meeting, the counterparts "celebrated the one-year anniversary of the Framework for our Major Defense Partnership and explored ways to strengthen cooperation." In a post on X, Pete Hegseth said, "Great meeting with Indian Minister of Defence Singh. We celebrated the one-year anniversary of the Framework for our Major Defense Partnership and explored ways to strengthen cooperation." The meeting comes as after the meeting in 2025, both leaders signed the ‘framework for the US-India major defence partnership’. The 2025 framework marked a new chapter to further transform the partnership over the next 10 years. According to the Ministry of Defence, it is intended to provide a unified vision and policy direction to deepen defence cooperation. Meanwhile, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth also met representatives from South Korea, Australia and Japan. For his meeting with South Korean Defence Minister Kang, he said, "Great meeting with ROK Minister of National Defense Kang at ADMM-Plus. The U.S.-ROK Alliance is built on peace through strength—ready forces, decisive capability, and combined lethality that deters aggression. America stands with allies that are serious about their own defense." For his meeting with Australian Deputy Prime Minister Marles, he said," It was a pleasure to meet with Australian Deputy Prime Minister Marles. Together, we are optimizing the Alliance to strengthen deterrence and deliver results." For his meeting with Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, he said, " I met with Japan’s Minister of Defense Shinjirō Koizumi @shinjirokoiz to advance our shared vision of peace through strength. Our strategic alignment is essential to building a credible denial defense—supported by increased investment, greater access, more realistic training, and stronger production of the munitions our forces need." The developments come as Rajnath Singh arrived in Cebu, on Tuesday night to attend the ADMM-Plus, where he will address shared regional and international security issues. Upon his arrival at Cebu airport, Singh received a ceremonial welcome from M Gen Fabian M Pedregosa PAF (Retd), Undersecretary of the Department of National Defence of the Philippines. Indian Ambassador to the Philippines Harsh Kumar Jain and Defence Attaché Captain ChandraKant Kothari were also present to welcome the Defence Minister. Singh later interacted with members of the Indian community and Filipino nationals upon arriving at his hotel. On Thursday, the Defence Minister will represent India at the ADMM-Plus meeting and address the forum on common regional and international security challenges. Before departing for Cebu, Singh reiterated India's commitment to strengthening its engagement with ASEAN and promoting stability across the Indo-Pacific region. In a post on X, he said, “India is firmly committed to ASEAN centrality and the peace, stability, and collective growth of the Indo-Pacific region under our Act East Policy.” On the sidelines of the meeting, Singh is scheduled to hold bilateral discussions with defence counterparts from several participating countries, including the host nation, the Philippines, as well as the United States, Japan, Australia, Singapore, Vietnam and South Korea. (ANI)

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab Devastates Uppada Beach Road; Restoration Teams Mobilised
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh: The vital 8-km Kakinada–Uppada Beach Road near Konapapapeta has been severely damaged after Very Severe Cyclone Arnab completed its landfall process along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday, at 2:00 AM.

Powerful tidal surges and intense coastal erosion completely washed away major portions of the scenic road, entirely severing connectivity to the local fishing harbour and dozens of nearby coastal villages.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) reported that the storm struck the coast with destructive winds gusting up to 150 kmph, bringing torrential rainfall to the East Godavari region.

State disaster management chief Prakhar Jain confirmed the widespread infrastructure damage, noting, "The cyclone brought heavy to very heavy rainfall, triggering widespread disruption in affected areas.
Damage assessments are fully underway".

While three casualties have been reported across the state due to separate tree and pole collapses, advance precautionary measures and the evacuation of over 76,000 residents helped prevent larger-scale human loss.
In an official statement, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu credited the administrative machinery, stating that advance safety plans successfully prevented extensive casualties.
The Andhra Pradesh state government has put the district on high alert and immediately deployed emergency restoration teams to repair the coastal artery.

stories.headline: Heavy rain alert for 9 Jharkhand districts amid cyclone Arnab
stories.title: Heavy rain alert for 9 Jharkhand districts amid cyclone Arnab
stories.summary: Ranchi, Oct 28 : Weather conditions have changed across Jharkhand under the influence of the severe cyclonic storm 'Arnab', which originated in the Bay of Bengal. Several parts of the state, including the capital Ranchi, have been witnessing rainfall since Wednesday morning, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to issue a heavy rainfall warning for nine districts. The IMD has warned of heavy rainfall in Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Bokaro, Seraikela-Kharsawan, and East and West Singhbhum districts. The impact of the cyclone is also expected to bring down temperatures across Jharkhand by around three to four degrees Celsius. In view of the prevailing weather conditions and the possibility of further deterioration, authorities have ordered the suspension of classes from kindergarten (KG) to Class 12 in Ranchi and Lohardaga districts on October 28 and 29 as a precautionary measure. In Ranchi, intermittent showers have continued since Wednesday morning, while the sky remains overcast. Rainfall accompanied by strong winds has brought a noticeable change in the weather, with temperatures dropping across the city. Similar conditions have been reported from several other parts of Jharkhand, including Hazaribagh, Koderma, Chaibasa, Deoghar, Giridih and Bokaro, where cloudy skies and rainfall have affected normal weather conditions. Meteorological Department scientist Abhishek Anand explained that Jharkhand's geographical location means the Singhbhum region is likely to experience the cyclone's effects first. Thereafter, rainfall and strong winds may spread to other parts of the state, depending on the storm's movement and intensity. The Meteorological Department has urged residents to remain vigilant, particularly in areas where heavy rainfall is expected. Cyclone 'Arnab' reached the Andhra Pradesh coast early Wednesday morning. According to the department's forecast, the cyclone was expected to cross the coast south of Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. During the landfall period, sustained wind speeds were projected to reach 125–135 kmph, while gusts could touch 150 kmph. Amid the changing weather conditions, Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri convened a meeting with officials from the departments concerned and issued directions to ensure preparedness and a prompt response to any weather-related emergencies. As part of the precautionary arrangements, the electricity department's control room and the Ranchi Municipal Corporation's rapid response team have been placed on alert. The teams have been instructed to respond immediately to incidents such as power supply disruptions and waterlogging caused by heavy rainfall or strong winds. The Railways has also initiated precautionary measures in anticipation of the cyclone's impact. According to information released by the Railways, the operations of at least half a dozen trains either originating from Jharkhand or passing through the state have been cancelled in view of the prevailing conditions. The administration has appealed to residents to take necessary precautions during thunderstorms and periods of strong winds. Commuters have also been urged to exercise caution while travelling on roads affected by waterlogging and to remain alert to changing conditions. The public has been asked to follow weather warnings issued by the Meteorological Department and comply with instructions from the local administration to minimise the risk of accidents and other emergencies. Farmers, meanwhile, have been advised to shift harvested crops and other agricultural produce to safe locations to protect them from rain and strong winds. --IANS

stories.headline: Andhra reports no casualties after cyclone Arnab, says CM Naidu
stories.title: Andhra reports no casualties after cyclone Arnab, says CM Naidu
stories.summary: Amaravati, Oct 28 : Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday said no loss of life has been reported so far following Cyclone Arnab, crediting advance precautionary measures taken by the administration for preventing casualties. Speaking during a teleconference with 32,000 personnel, including district collectors, the Chief Minister directed officials to minimise property damage and restore normalcy in cyclone-affected areas at the earliest. "No loss of life has been reported so far due to Cyclone Arnab. The advance precautionary measures taken by the administrative machinery helped prevent casualties," said Naidu in an official press release. The CM instructed officials to clear roads blocked by fallen trees within two hours and ensure immediate removal of trees obstructing national highways. Also, he directed them to restore electricity supply in affected areas once strong winds subsided. Naidu stressed the need to provide adequate food, drinking water and medical facilities at cyclone shelters and asked officials to prevent water from entering agricultural fields, protect horticultural crops and take measures to prevent breaches in tanks and canals. The CM asked officials to prepare preliminary estimates of crop damage and keep National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel on standby. Further, the officials were directed to make full use of the Manamitra system to address public grievances in cyclone-affected areas and ensure that complainants were informed about the action taken to resolve their issues. Meanwhile, Kakinada Superintendent of Police (SP) G Bindu Madhav said, "Cyclone Arnab had significantly affected the district, uprooting a few hundred trees and fewer than 100 electric poles. However, no major damage has been reported and rainfall subsided after 1 am." Madhav said people were evacuated to relief camps as a precautionary measure and remained there due to the strong winds and roar of the storm between midnight and 1 am. The Uppada road, running along the coast, has been completely washed away, he said, adding that rainfall was relatively low in the district with gusty winds causing the main impact. Alluri Sitaramaraju district SP Amit Bardar said the Cyclone had limited impact on the district, as of 9 am, with trees and electric poles uprooted and some roads inundated. "No loss of life or major damage to infrastructure, houses or livestock has been reported so far. We are monitoring the situation closely as water levels may rise due to continued rainfall," Bardar told PTI. An old bridge in Tadiguda village of Anantagiri mandal was washed away, isolating a hamlet, said the SP, adding that alternative arrangements were being made and restoration work was underway. The preliminary assessment indicated limited overall impact, though the situation would continue to be monitored as rainfall persisted, he added. Konaseema district SP Rahul Meena said gusty winds reaching up 130 kmph had uprooted trees and electric poles across the district during the Cyclone late on Tuesday night. No casualties or property damage had been reported. Fallen trees and electric poles had blocked roads and disrupted power supply, he said, adding that electricity connections were expected to be restored by within few hours, while major highways would be cleared within two to three hours. "Konaseema is among the worst-affected districts, with winds reaching up to 130 kmph uprooting trees and electric poles, blocking roads and disrupting power supply," the SP told PTI. Clearance of interior roads could take until evening, he said, adding that wind speeds had reduced and the cyclone had moved towards Kakinada after weakening slightly. More than 10,000 people had been evacuated from low-lying areas and shifted to shelters, according to his preliminary information. Around 495 cyclone shelters and temporary relief centres had been set up. No village inundation had been reported and water accumulated due to the storm surge had drained, he said. Two NDRF teams and as many SDRF teams were deployed a day before the cyclone to conduct road clearance and rescue operations in response to emergency calls, he said. Additional Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) platoons had also been deployed for clearance operations and other tasks, he said, adding that personnel from various departments were working continuously to restore normalcy by evening. PTI

stories.title: Rain likely in Delhi-NCR till Nov 1 due to Cyclone Arnab; pollution levels turn poor

article_sentences: The cyclone is expected to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 125-135 kmph, gusting to 150 kmph, the IMD said in a press release.

New Delhi: Delhi-NCR is likely to witness a change in weather conditions, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting isolated to scattered rainfall across the national capital from October 28 to November 1 under the influence of a western disturbance and very severe Cyclone Arnab.
The unseasonal rainfall is expected to bring a significant drop in daytime temperatures, potentially affecting Karwa Chauth celebrations.
The forecast comes as northern and eastern India brace for rainfall over the coming days.

According to the IMD, a western disturbance, in the form of a cyclonic circulation, lies over northwest Uttar Pradesh and its neighbourhood, influencing weather conditions across parts of north India.

Meanwhile, Cyclone Arnab is likely to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm by the forenoon of October 28.
The weather agency has also forecast isolated to very heavy rainfall over Telangana and Vidarbha on October 28, followed by Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha on October 29.
Bihar is likely to experience rainfall between October 29 and 30.

Meanwhile, Delhi's air quality remained in the 'poor' category on Wednesday morning, with the city-level Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching 250 at 8 a.m., according to the Central Pollution Control Board's (CPCB) All India AQI portal.
PM2.5, fine particulate matter capable of penetrating deep into the lungs, was identified as the prominent pollutant.
Among the monitoring stations, Vivek Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 320, followed by Jahangirpuri at 307 and Patparganj at 291.
Sirifort recorded an AQI of 290, while Dwarka Sector 8 registered 286.

stories.headline: Assam Launches Massive Green Recovery Drive: 2.4 Lakh Saplings Distributed to Flood-Hit Farmers
stories.title: Assam Launches Massive Green Recovery Drive: 2.4 Lakh Saplings Distributed to Flood-Hit Farmers
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Sivasagar — In a major push toward climate resilience and economic rehabilitation, the Assam Government has distributed approximately 2.4 lakh high-yielding coconut and arecanut seedlings to flood-affected farmers.
The distribution drive, targeting the severely hit Sivasagar and Charaideo districts, aims to help over 50,000 farmers recover from devastating monsoon damages.

Handing over the saplings at a public event at the Boarding Playground, Agriculture and Irrigation Minister Pijush Hazarika detailed the state's vision to transform Assam into a horticultural powerhouse.
The initial phase delivered 80,000 coconut and 1.6 lakh arecanut plants to promote immediate crop diversification.
State-wide, the annual target stands at 2.84 lakh coconut and 8 lakh arecanut saplings.
Minister Hazarika announced that the government is aggressively working to double its active irrigation network, significantly reducing agrarian dependence on erratic rainfall.

Flanked by Water Resources Minister Susanta Borgohain and MLA Akhil Gogoi, Hazarika also assured farmers that adequate seeds and technical inputs are secured for the upcoming Rabi cropping season to guarantee sustainable rural livelihoods.

stories.headline: Israel election: exit polls point to no clear winner or majority
stories.title: Israel election: exit polls point to no clear winner or majority
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 28 : Israel's parliamentary election appeared to have produced no clear winner, with exit polls indicating that both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition alliance seeking to replace him had fallen short of the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. According to The Jerusalem Post, the exit polls projected Netanyahu's bloc to secure 51-52 seats, while the opposition bloc, comprising Yashar, B'Yachad, Yisrael Beytenu and the Democrats, was expected to win 49-51 seats. Channels 11 and 13 projected both sides to be tied at 51 seats each, while Channel 12's survey gave Netanyahu's bloc a slight edge with 52 seats. The opposition bloc declared victory shortly after the exit poll results were released, although neither side appeared to have a clear route to forming a government. The exit polls also indicated that the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former chief of staff of the Israel Defence Forces, could emerge with a slight advantage over Netanyahu's right-wing and far-right coalition in terms of the combined strength of its constituent parties. However, Netanyahu's Likud was projected to remain the single largest party, with around 27 seats, while Yashar was forecast to win 21-22 seats. The results suggested that Netanyahu continued to retain the support of a substantial core of Likud voters despite widespread opposition to his leadership among sections of the Israeli electorate. Nevertheless, the projected seat distribution indicated that his ability to form another coalition government could be constrained by the opposition's combined strength and the potential influence of smaller parties. The election witnessed a historic voter turnout and was described by some as one of the most consequential in Israel's history. It was also marked by record participation among Israeli Arab voters, adding another significant dimension to the electoral contest. Exit polls projected that Israeli Arab parties could collectively secure as many as 18 seats in the Knesset, potentially giving them considerable leverage during the negotiations to form the next government. Their projected strength could make them kingmakers in what is expected to be a prolonged coalition-building process, particularly if Netanyahu's bloc fails to gather the support required to reach the majority threshold, according to The Guardian. With neither camp appearing to have a straightforward path to the required 61 seats, the final distribution of seats and the positions adopted by smaller parties were expected to play a decisive role in determining the next government. Voter turnout in Israel's parliamentary election on Tuesday reached 77.7 per cent of eligible voters by the time polling stations closed at 10 p.m. local time, according to the final update from Israel's Central Elections Committee, which oversees the vote. The turnout was the highest recorded in an Israeli election in 27 years, exceeding the 2022 figure by more than seven percentage points. --IANS

Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) has announced the decision to reschedul polling and counting for the MPTC and ZPTC elections, amid the shortage of police personnel and polling staff.
The polling, which is supposed to be held on 3 November, will now be held on 5 November from 7am to 5pm.
Re-polling, if required, will be held on 6 November.
Meanwhile, counting has been postponed from 5 November to 7 November and will begin at 8am, with results to be declared as soon as counting is complete.
The changes were made because the counting of municipal election votes coincides with Parishad election polling.
The SEC said the revised schedule would help ensure staff and other resources are used efficiently.
State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha also announced that voting at 88 polling stations in Alluri Sitarama Raju and Polavaram districts will end at 3pm.

Suri Payala has contended that records obtained from the Legislative Department show that the material placed before the Search Committee and the Selection Committee consisted primarily of lists of candidates, service particulars, dates and service records.

He argues that the records do not show a specific assessment of whether the candidates possessed experience in the conduct of elections or satisfied the requirement relating to integrity.
According to the application, the minutes of the selection process refer to candidates being considered on the basis of their eligibility and experience.
However, the petitioner alleges that the underlying records do not disclose any specific exercise to ascertain their election-related experience or integrity.
He further contends that merely recording that Section 5 was noted, without disclosing how its requirements were assessed, does not demonstrate compliance with the statutory framework.

With respect to the appointments of Gyanesh Kumar and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu as ECs made on March 14, 2024, the petitioner has questioned the process through which the Search Committee shortlisted candidates for two vacancies.

stories.title: Over 1 lakh voter cases cloud Kolkata civic polls as Opposition questions election timeline

article_sentences: The State Election Commission has released draft rolls for 209 newly delimited KMC wards, but Opposition parties have questioned the November 12 deadline amid concerns over more than one lakh voter cases.

Kolkata: Nearly 32 lakh voters, 209 newly delimited wards, and more than one lakh disputed voter cases have put Kolkata’s municipal election preparations under scrutiny, with Opposition parties questioning whether the electoral machinery has enough time to resolve discrepancies before it publishes the final rolls.

The State Election Commission has circulated draft electoral rolls and proposed polling-station layouts for all 209 wards of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), setting November 12 as the deadline for filing claims and objections.
However, the release of the draft documents has done little to ease concerns over voter verification, pending tribunal cases and the impact of electoral-roll revisions.
The controversy has also brought election timing into sharper focus.

Opposition parties have sought to postpone the civic polls, arguing that the exercise should not proceed until the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process and the Special Summary Revision announced by the Election Commission of India are complete.

The draft rolls and proposed booth arrangements were presented to political parties at the New Administrative Building in Alipore by senior officials of the South 24-Parganas district administration, led by the additional district magistrate.
The draft electoral rolls cover nearly 32 lakh voters across the 209 wards.

While the publication marks a step towards preparing for the civic elections, Opposition representatives have questioned whether the schedule allows sufficient time to scrutinise the changes and establish the status of voters whose cases remain unresolved.
Their concerns centre on the combined workload arising from ward delimitation, voter-roll revision and the allocation of polling stations.
With November 12 as the deadline, parties argue that officials must verify voter movements, identify discrepancies and address pending appeals within a compressed timeframe.
They have described examining the changes and correcting thousands of discrepancies in just over two weeks as logistically impossible.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court directed the EC to allow voters who had not submitted their enumeration forms or had shifted residences to complete the process, including by submitting Form 8 for address changes.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday questioned whether the Election Commission (EC) had "applied its mind" while excluding voters from Delhi's draft electoral roll during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
It asked why people whose names featured in the 2026 voter list were being asked to fill Form 6 as new voters after shifting addresses.

The top court also directed the poll panel to allow voters who had not submitted their enumeration forms or had shifted residences to complete the process, including by submitting Form 8 for address changes.
The EC assured the bench that the October 30 deadline for filing claims and objections would be extended.
During the hearing, the bench raised concerns over the treatment of voters who may have been temporarily away from their registered addresses when Booth Level.
Officers (BLOs) visited to distribute enumeration forms.
It questioned whether failing to submit the form within the stipulated period could be grounds for permanently denying someone the right to vote.
"Right to vote is a vital act," Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed, questioning whether a voter who failed to return an enumeration form on time should lose the right to re-enter the electoral rolls.

The bench also asked the EC why someone whose name was already on the 2026 electoral roll but had subsequently shifted residence was being asked to fill Form 6, which is meant for new voter registration.

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant asked the EC to explain why such voters could not instead use Form 8, which is meant for shifting residence within a constituency or from one constituency to another.
Justice Bagchi said Forms 6, 7 and 8 were prescribed under the law and could not be altered.

stories.headline: Can Major League Baseball hit a home run in cricket’s own country?
stories.title: Can Major League Baseball hit a home run in cricket’s own country?
stories.summary: Nick Swisher, a Major League Baseball (MLB) World Series champion and All-Star, is full of beans about his first visit to India. “The furthest I’d travelled until now is Dubai. I’m thrilled to have come this far,” says Swisher, high-fiving and bouncing his way through the media rounds, unfazed by Mumbai’s sultry October heat.While Swisher discovers India for the first time, MLB has its sights set on a much bigger prize: Growing its footprint in the country. As it looks to build momentum, the North American baseball league brought its former stars and Indian cricketers together on October 24 for the maiden edition of MLBx: A time-controlled, 3x3, mixed-gender contest.At Mumbai’s Andheri Sports Complex, on a ballpark fashioned out of a football field, Swisher turned out with fellow All-Stars Jake Arrieta and Adrian Gonzalez and 2013 World Series champion Jonny Gomes, joining cricketers Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Deepak Chahar and Radha Yadav, among others, in teams of three, with a singular objective: To outdo one another in home runs, the sport’s most explosive and celebrated hit.This isn’t MLB’s first tango with cricket, though. In 2023, the league signed England cricketers Harry Brook and Issy Wong as its European ambassadors. Brook, a swashbuckling batter, even joined the St Louis Cardinals for a training session in Florida. But the league’s India challenge will be way tougher—it will involve making inroads into a country where cricket dominates national mindspace, and where baseball has resonated only sporadically through cultural riffs like Billy Joel’s iconic We Didn’t Start the Fire (Joe DiMaggio) or films such as Moneyball and A League of Their Own.Also Read: From Mumbai to Goa, and Jharkhand to Kerala, the growing popularity of pickleball in IndiaAccording to WPP Media’s Sporting Nation 2025 report, cricket accounted for 89 percent of the sports industry’s revenues, cornering 81 percent of sponsorship spends, 87 percent of endorsements and 95 percent of media costs. And getting a toehold in that landscape will require MLB to swing much harder than bringing India’s T20 World-Cup-winning captain Yadav on board as its first-ever Indian brand ambassador.Jeremiah Yolkut, senior vice president, global operations and events, MLB, however, sees cricket not as baseball’s rival but as its launchpad. “India has a large young population, a growing sports and entertainment market, and significant economic potential. Baseball and cricket also share fundamental similarities, which gives us a natural starting point to introduce the sport to new audiences. This is a long-term investment—we’re thinking five to 10 years ahead, not just about a single event or season,” Yolkut tells Forbes India in an emailed interview from New York. (Standing L to R) Jonny Gomes, Suryakumar Yadav, Shardul Thakur, Jordan Woolery, Adrian Gonzalez and Jake Arrieta; (Sitting L to R) Deepak Chahar, Jitesh Sharma, Rachel Garcia, Nick Swisher, Kashvee Gautam and Radha Yadav Photo Courtesy MLBxWith India’s sports economy at Rs1.99 lakh crore in FY26, as a recent KPMG report states, and growing at 12 to 14 percent annually, it’s no surprise that the country remains a lucrative market for foreign sports leagues. And MLB, which set up an office in New Delhi in 2019, is no exception. In seven years, Yolkut claims to have taken baseball to over 20,000 students, penetrating the grassroots through the MLB Youth Cup that now features 150 teams with 1,800 players.“But grassroots alone is only half the equation. Having an on-ground presence and school-level participation forms the bedrock of familiarity. If you want to scale in a market as dynamic as India, you have to build beyond the game,” says Vinit Karnik, managing director, content, sports & entertainment, WPP Media South Asia. And baseball knows it well enough, having taken a few swings at India earlier as well.BASEBALL’S MANY INNINGSIn 2008, Los Angeles sports agent JB Bernstein brought to India a pitching contest that was won by two Uttar Pradesh boys—Rinku Singh and Dinesh Patel. Both travelled to the US to play baseball, and their story was later turned into a biographical film in 2014, Million Dollar Arm, starring Jon Hamm. Neither eventually made it to the elite tier, making only minor league appearances, but MLB’s India connection was rekindled once again when Arjun Nimmala, a first-generation Indian-American from Florida, was selected as a top prospect for the Toronto Blue Jays in 2023. Next year, pitcher Kumar Rocker became the first player of Indian descent to debut in the league (for the Texas Rangers). Earlier this year, Maharashtrian Akshay More was signed by Japan’s Saitama Seibu Lions as a development player in the Nippon Professional League, marking another stride ahead for the sport in India.Also Read: Turning interest into fandom is our goal for women’s football: Jinisha Sharma“We’ve also invested in storytelling as well, including our Indian Baseball Dreams documentary in 2023 (on Nimmala) and the Hot Shots hitting competition in 2024, featuring cricketer Shikhar Dhawan and former MLB player Adam Jones,” says Yolkut. “That said, our strategy isn’t built around a handful of individual players. It's about developing a broader ecosystem for baseball in India.”To that end, MLB is taking a leaf out of cricket’s playbook where the ICC (International Cricket Council), its governing body, has used T20—the sport’s shortest, most exciting iteration—as a vehicle to take the game beyond its stronghold. The baseball league is following a similar script with MLBx, with a three-player, three-inning, 30-minute contest instead of the traditional nine innings. The format has already been played at 15 US venues in the past three years as well as international destinations like London (UK), Seoul (South Korea) and Mexico City (Mexico), and is set to debut in Japan (at Fukuoka) in November. Nick Swisher signs autographs for an enthusiastic crowd at the MLBx event. Photo Courtesy MLBxMLBx also borrows from the sport-plus-entertainment template popularised by the IPL (Indian Premier League), interspersing the three matches in Mumbai with DJ sets and performances by rappers Kr$na and Badshah, and setting up food kiosks as well as batting cages for fans to have a go. “It is positioned as a high-energy sports and entertainment experience. The focus is on younger, urban sports and entertainment audiences, including people discovering baseball for the first time. The pitch is about audience relevance, brand integration and the overall consumer experience—not just the sport itself,” says Nikhil Bardia, head, Rise Worldwide, the on-ground partner for MLB.Its crossover into the music and the entertainment ecosystem is evident from the fact that almost two out of three people who bought tickets for the event were buying a sports ticket on BookMyShow, the ticketing partner, for the first time. "Around half of them had previously booked a live entertainment experience with us, most often music and comedy. The audience also showed a clear willingness to pay for a premium experience, with the Lounge Hospitality tier selling out more than a week before the event and the on-field catching zone selling out entirely,” says Anil Makhija, COO-live entertainment and venues, BookMyShow. He adds that while the gameplay was at the centre, the additional touchpoints that MLBx created through food, hospitality, interactive experiences, merchandise, what have you, made the sport more accessible, encouraging participation and discovery.Globally, leagues such as the NBA have built fanbases by extending their appeal beyond the court and into fashion and lifestyle. Basketball stars—from Michael Jordan and Shaquille O’Neal to LeBron James, Kobe Bryant and Allen Iverson—have been known to sport statement outfits that have shaped popular trends. Jordan’s partnership with Nike, which began in his rookie season in 1984 and led to the launch of the Air Jordan line, arguably defined sneaker culture and continues to pay him millions in royalties. And the rise of the NBA has been intrinsically intertwined with the rise of hip-hop, with the two sharing spaces, lingo and each amplifying the aesthetics of the other.“In baseball too, the Savannah Bananas, a professional team launched in the US in 2016, has introduced a fast-paced version of the game that replaces the traditional format with entertainment, music and showmanship—just like T20 cricket. It shows how baseball is reinventing itself to make itself appealing to newer constituencies,” says Hemant Dua, founder of Inspiranti Sports and advisor to GMR Sports.Also Read: Match Ball: How Anahat Singh is fast-tracking India's Olympics dream in squashIt also proves how modern leagues must live at the intersection of sport and culture. “For a league like MLB to make a genuine dent, it needs to tap into contemporary Indian pop culture: Leveraging music, lifestyle and cross-sport appeal with icons like Yadav. When an Indian consumer sees someone they revere engaging with baseball, it creates a cultural bridge that a grassroots clinic alone cannot build,” says Karnik of WPP Media South Asia.THE LONG HAULBut how does one ensure that an event like MLBx returns for a second and third edition, and that the sport gains firmer ground in newer geographies each time? By shifting from an event mindset to a multi-layered ecosystem mindset, backed by patience, says Karnik.Touchpoints like MLBx can be hugely catalytic for baseball, while the presence of the cricketers can bring eyeballs and familiarity. But invoking similar playing mechanics—throwing a ball, hitting it with a bat and fielding it—will not necessarily translate into the growth of the sport. The experience of MLC, the franchise cricket league in the US, is a case in point: Its launch in 2023 has yet to trigger a culture shift that brings baseball fans to watch the game. “You need accessibility, viewership, grassroots and community as interconnected pillars to build an enduring sports culture,” Karnik adds.Also Read: Running is the fastest growing sporting activity in India: Anil and Vivek SinghDua, who headed MLC team Seattle Orcas until last year, confirms that cricket in the US remains largely diaspora-driven, with crossovers still minimal despite the MLC typing up with local baseball players to engender familiarity. “The one thing I can say with confidence is that whoever from baseball has come and seen T20 has been hooked. But has there been a shift in the US? I’d say no,” he says. “MLB, too, will have to go through the hard yards in India before it establishes itself here.”While MLB is looking at the IPL model, it shouldn’t expect success to come overnight. When the IPL started in 2008, cricket was already a national religion. Even then, it took years—and the convergence of cheap mobile data, rising smartphone penetration and a deliberate push towards regionality through local languages—for the league to grow into the phenomenon it is today and for its value to touch $20.6 billion (according to US-based investment bank Houlihan Lokey). “Ideally, MLB should start to build small, local connections. There is great scope that can be deeply penetrated. MLB can’t turn baseball into a full-fledged property immediately, but with MLBx, it can try and build that intensity slowly, with a lot of local anchoring,” says Saurabh Arora, chief commercial officer of IPL franchise Punjab Kings.The emergence of the Pro Kabaddi League has shown that Indian audiences have an appetite for a ‘second sport’. The league extricated kabaddi from its rural roots and relative obscurity, attracting 201 million viewers in its 11th season in 2024 and making it the most-watched sports league after the IPL and WPL (Women’s Premier League). Central to that transformation was the way the game was repackaged in a fast-paced TV-friendly format, built around a ticking clock, aimed at providing a dopamine hit—a cocktail that MLBx, too, offers. “But it's not just viewership, MLB will need participation from schools, colleges too to make the sport popular,” says Arora of Punjab Kings. “Realistically, I feel it will be a seven-to-10-year build.”What MLB needs to do in India, suggests Dua, is find that one Indian player who becomes a catalyst for the sport—much like Yao Ming, an eight-time All-Star and Hall of Famer, did for the NBA in China. The 7-foot-6 basketball star’s arrival in the NBA with the Houston Rockets in 2002 helped propel the league’s popularity in his home country, with the NBA reaching 765 million unique viewers in China by 2015, four years after Ming retired.While that number is far-fetched for MLB as of now, “even if they can get 10 to 20 million people watching in India, they would have grown an audience as good as Japan or South Korea”, Dua says. “From a population point of view, you've captured literally one country with not a lot of effort.”In the years ahead, it will be a home run as good as any.

The pitch is about audience relevance, brand integration and the overall consumer experience—not just the sport itself,” says Nikhil Bardia, head, Rise Worldwide, the on-ground partner for MLB.

Its crossover into the music and the entertainment ecosystem is evident from the fact that almost two out of three people who bought tickets for the event were buying a sports ticket on BookMyShow, the ticketing partner, for the first time.
"Around half of them had previously booked a live entertainment experience with us, most often music and comedy.

The audience also showed a clear willingness to pay for a premium experience, with the Lounge Hospitality tier selling out more than a week before the event and the on-field catching zone selling out entirely,” says Anil Makhija, COO-live entertainment and venues, BookMyShow.

He adds that while the gameplay was at the centre, the additional touchpoints that MLBx created through food, hospitality, interactive experiences, merchandise, what have you, made the sport more accessible, encouraging participation and discovery.
Globally, leagues such as the NBA have built fanbases by extending their appeal beyond the court and into fashion and lifestyle.
Basketball stars—from Michael Jordan and Shaquille O’Neal to LeBron James, Kobe Bryant and Allen Iverson—have been known to sport statement outfits that have shaped popular trends.
And the rise of the NBA has been intrinsically intertwined with the rise of hip-hop, with the two sharing spaces, lingo and each amplifying the aesthetics of the other.

“In baseball too, the Savannah Bananas, a professional team launched in the US in 2016, has introduced a fast-paced version of the game that replaces the traditional format with entertainment, music and showmanship—just like T20 cricket.
It shows how baseball is reinventing itself to make itself appealing to newer constituencies,” says Hemant Dua, founder of Inspiranti Sports and advisor to GMR Sports.
It also proves how modern leagues must live at the intersection of sport and culture.
“For a league like MLB to make a genuine dent, it needs to tap into contemporary Indian pop culture: Leveraging music, lifestyle and cross-sport appeal with icons like Yadav.
When an Indian consumer sees someone they revere engaging with baseball, it creates a cultural bridge that a grassroots clinic alone cannot build,” says Karnik of WPP Media South Asia.
THE LONG HAULBut how does one ensure that an event like MLBx returns for a second and third edition, and that the sport gains firmer ground in newer geographies each time?
By shifting from an event mindset to a multi-layered ecosystem mindset, backed by patience, says Karnik.
Touchpoints like MLBx can be hugely catalytic for baseball, while the presence of the cricketers can bring eyeballs and familiarity.
But invoking similar playing mechanics—throwing a ball, hitting it with a bat and fielding it—will not necessarily translate into the growth of the sport.
The experience of MLC, the franchise cricket league in the US, is a case in point: Its launch in 2023 has yet to trigger a culture shift that brings baseball fans to watch the game.
“You need accessibility, viewership, grassroots and community as interconnected pillars to build an enduring sports culture,” Karnik adds.

Dua, who headed MLC team Seattle Orcas until last year, confirms that cricket in the US remains largely diaspora-driven, with crossovers still minimal despite the MLC typing up with local baseball players to engender familiarity.
“The one thing I can say with confidence is that whoever from baseball has come and seen T20 has been hooked.
But has there been a shift in the US?
I’d say no,” he says.
“MLB, too, will have to go through the hard yards in India before it establishes itself here.” While MLB is looking at the IPL model, it shouldn’t expect success to come overnight.
When the IPL started in 2008, cricket was already a national religion.

Even then, it took years—and the convergence of cheap mobile data, rising smartphone penetration and a deliberate push towards regionality through local languages—for the league to grow into the phenomenon it is today and for its value to touch $20.6 billion (according to US-based investment bank Houlihan Lokey).
“Ideally, MLB should start to build small, local connections.
There is great scope that can be deeply penetrated.

MLB can’t turn baseball into a full-fledged property immediately, but with MLBx, it can try and build that intensity slowly, with a lot of local anchoring,” says Saurabh Arora, chief commercial officer of IPL franchise Punjab Kings.
The emergence of the Pro Kabaddi League has shown that Indian audiences have an appetite for a ‘second sport’.

The league extricated kabaddi from its rural roots and relative obscurity, attracting 201 million viewers in its 11th season in 2024 and making it the most-watched sports league after the IPL and WPL (Women’s Premier League).

Central to that transformation was the way the game was repackaged in a fast-paced TV-friendly format, built around a ticking clock, aimed at providing a dopamine hit—a cocktail that MLBx, too, offers.
“But it's not just viewership, MLB will need participation from schools, colleges too to make the sport popular,” says Arora of Punjab Kings.

“Realistically, I feel it will be a seven-to-10-year build.” What MLB needs to do in India, suggests Dua, is find that one Indian player who becomes a catalyst for the sport—much like Yao Ming, an eight-time All-Star and Hall of Famer, did for the NBA in China.
While that number is far-fetched for MLB as of now, “even if they can get 10 to 20 million people watching in India, they would have grown an audience as good as Japan or South Korea”, Dua says.
“From a population point of view, you've captured literally one country with not a lot of effort.” In the years ahead, it will be a home run as good as any.

stories.headline: CERC Proposes Allowing Pumped Storage Plants to Participate in High-Price Power Market
stories.title: CERC Proposes Allowing Pumped Storage Plants to Participate in High-Price Power Market
stories.summary: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has proposed allowing pumped storage plants (PSPs) to participate in the High Price Day Ahead Market (HP-DAM), potentially providing storage developers with an additional avenue to sell electricity during periods of high demand and prices. In an order, the commission proposed including PSPs as an eligible category of generating stations in the existing HP-DAM segment on power exchanges. The commission has initiated suo motu proceedings on the proposal and invited written submissions from parties within 15 days of the order. The proposal follows recommendations from the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC) and a suggestion from the Ministry of Power to consider allowing PSPs to participate in the high-price market segment. CERC said the existing Day Ahead Market (DAM) alone may not provide sufficient commercial opportunities for pumped storage projects under prevailing market conditions. Participation in HP-DAM could improve their commercial viability by allowing them to access periods of higher demand and prices. The commission also noted that greater participation by pumped storage plants could improve the utilisation of flexible storage resources during periods of constrained power supply, supporting grid flexibility. India has 7.4 GW of operational pumped storage capacity According to an analysis submitted by NLDC, India had 7,425.6 MW of operational pumped storage capacity, comprising 4,845.6 MW of on-stream projects and 2,580 MW of off-stream projects, based on a Central Electricity Authority (CEA) report published in January 2026. Another 15,870 MW of PSP capacity was under construction, while the country's estimated pumped storage potential stood at approximately 290.2 GW. NLDC noted that operational pumped storage plants were almost fully tied up, leaving limited merchant capacity among operational inter-state transmission system-connected projects. Allowing PSPs with merchant capacity to participate in HP-DAM could provide an additional market for energy arbitrage during periods of high-price discovery. ALSO READ: Australia Walks Away From 7.2 GWh of Pumped Hydro. India Is Planning 100 GW Solar and evening peak prices offer arbitrage opportunity The commission's proposal is supported by NLDC's analysis of market-clearing prices between April 2025 and July 2026, which identified a substantial difference between electricity prices during solar generation hours and evening peak demand. According to the analysis, average unconstrained market-clearing prices in the Day Ahead Market were approximately ₹2.20 per unit during solar hours and ₹6.57 per unit during evening peak hours. The resulting price differential of around ₹4.37 per unit indicates a potential arbitrage opportunity for pumped storage projects, subject to project-specific costs and operating conditions. Pumped storage plants use electricity to pump water to an upper reservoir when power is relatively inexpensive and generate electricity by releasing the stored water when demand and prices are higher. However, NLDC's analysis also highlighted the limited liquidity of the existing HP-DAM segment. Between April 2025 and July 2026, market clearing occurred on 47 days, or 9.65% of the analysis period, and across 965 time blocks, accounting for 2.06% of the period. While HP-DAM recorded higher price discovery than the regular DAM during certain intervals, the commission noted that actual revenue realisation would depend on both the prices discovered and the volume of electricity successfully cleared. Pumped storage costs could affect commercial viability NLDC's assessment also examined the costs associated with pumped storage projects. The levelised fixed-cost component of PSP tariffs was estimated at approximately ₹3.30-4.98 per unit, while the effective landed tariff, including pumping costs, could reach ₹8.92 per unit, depending on project-specific characteristics and operating assumptions. The order cited several examples of approved or discovered tariffs, including ₹6.69 per unit for Greenko's 500 MW/3,000 MWh standalone storage project awarded by NTPC Renewable Energy Ltd in December 2022, based on the effective storage cost under a two charge-discharge cycle operation. These figures indicate that the commercial case for participation in high-price markets will depend on project costs, pumping expenses, market prices and the availability of trading opportunities. CERC initiates proceedings on proposed inclusion HP-DAM was introduced under the Integrated Day Ahead Market framework to provide a trading avenue for generating stations with high generation costs that could face constraints under the prevailing price ceiling in the regular DAM. The eligible categories currently include gas-based generating stations using imported regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) and naphtha, imported coal-based generating stations using only imported coal, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). The Ministry of Power's guidelines for promoting pumped storage projects, issued in April 2023, had provided for PSPs and other storage projects to participate in all power exchange market segments, including HP-DAM, to take advantage of price differences between peak and off-peak periods. CERC's latest order proposes extending the existing eligibility framework to pumped storage plants. The commission has directed parties to submit their written representations within 15 days, with further proceedings to follow under Regulation 56 of the Conduct of Business Regulations, 2023.

stories.headline: India, Mexico begin talks on new Preferential Trade Agreement
stories.title: India, Mexico begin talks on new Preferential Trade Agreement
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 28 : The government on Wednesday said India and Mexico have taken a decisive step towards a stronger economic partnership with the signing of the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) between the two nations. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal and Luis Rosendo Gutierrez Romano, Mexico’s Undersecretary of Foreign Trade, formally launched the trade negotiations. “Our shared ambition: expand trade, unlock investment, strengthen supply chains and create new opportunities for businesses in both countries,” the Department of Commerce said in a statement on X. India and Mexico are ready to turn untapped potential into tangible prosperity through balanced, ambitious and mutually beneficial negotiations, the statement added. The proposed India-Mexico trade agreement is expected to cover key Indian exports, including automobiles, textiles, footwear, plastics, steel, chemicals and toys, which face tariffs of up to 50 per cent under Mexico’s new tariff regime. According to official trade data, India’s merchandise exports to Mexico stood at $5.73 billion in 2025-26, with automobiles accounting for the largest share at $1.92 billion. The Commerce Secretary arrived in Mexico City for a two-day official visit to advance trade and economic ties. He held a fruitful discussion with Fernando Gonzalez Saiffe, Director General for Asia-Pacific, Secretaria de Relaciones Exteriores (SRE), on India-Mexico relations and opportunities to learn from each other through mutual cooperation, leveraging our respective strengths and advancements. He appreciated Mexico’s keen interest in strengthening political exchanges and reaffirmed India’s shared commitment to mutual growth and prosperity. Agrawal highlighted the strong complementarities between the two economies, India’s robust growth of around 7 per cent, and the vast untapped potential for trade, investment and business partnerships. The PTA offers an opportunity to unlock new avenues of economic cooperation, strengthen business linkages, and build bridges across the Pacific towards shared prosperity, he observed. The Commerce Secretary also engaged with Indian and Mexican business leaders to explore opportunities, address challenges and deepen trade and investment ties. --IANS
